To trigger the `assert()`, it is enough that the first output byte is `'\b'`, `:!echo -en '\x08'|cat -`.

Researching this issue I tried running the command `echo -en '\x08test'|cat -` to see it's behavior in different environments.

OS X 10.10.5 zsh 5.0.5 connected via iTerm 2.1.1 and Terminal 2.5.3: 'test' printed on current row, followed by '%', newline then prompt.

OS X 10.10.5 Bash 3.2.57 connected via iTerm 2.1.1 and Terminal 2.5.3: 'test' printed on current row, followed directly by prompt. 

Gentoo 2.2 Bash 4.3.42 connected via iTerm 2.1.1 and Terminal 2.5.3: 'test' printed on current row, followed directly by prompt. 

Gentoo 2.2 Bash 4.3.42 connected via Prompt 2 for iOS: cursor moved to the previous row and the last column, printed 't' then moved to the next row, first column and printed 'est' followed directly by prompt.

issue.title: Zero width control characters insert spaces with shell ex commands

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
- Neovim version: 9a3b7fa90
- Operating system: Gentoo 2.2
- Terminal emulator: iTerm 2.1.1 (connected to remote system)

Discovered while researching https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/4142 and https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/2958

Running a shell command that echoes multiple bell symbols followed by text shifts text to the right.
### Actual behaviour

Text preceded by zero width control bell character is shifted to the right.
### Expected behaviour

Text should start in the first column.
### Steps to reproduce

```
nvim -u NONE
:!echo -en '\x07\x07\x07\x07text'
// prints
    text
// instead of
text
```

vim 7.4.769 with same configuration exhibits expected behavior

TODO:

- [x] handle bell chars "\x07" #4338 (with #7844, bell chars are printed as `^G`)
- [x] investigate relation to #1776 (conclusion: unrelated)

If a binary or other output is read from `:!` the screen should not be
affected by accidental (or intentional) control chars.
Legacy Vim `:!` gets scrubbed (possibly by canonical ("cooked")
mode in mch_call_shell(), see settmode(TMODE_COOK)).

Expected behavior:

```
:!echo -en '\x08'|cat -             " empty (except "Press ENTER")
:!echo -en '\x08'                   " empty (except "Press ENTER")
:!echo -en '\n'                     " extra line
:echo system('echo -en ''\x08\n''') " ^H

Issue #4338
:!echo -en '\x07\x07\x07\x07text'   " 'text' (not '    text')

Issue #2958 (Vim tputs()?)
:!echo -e "1\t2\t3"                 " '1       2       3'
```

~~Closes #5442~~ closed by #6618
~~Closes #4142~~ closed by #6618
Closes #2958 [WIP]
Closes #4338 [WIP]

issue.body:
This will crash nvim 0.1.6 (and probably much older):

```
:!cat build/bin/nvim
src/nvim/ui.c:507: ui_cursor_left: Assertion `new_col >= 0` failed
```

This isn't a super important problem given that the "normal" behavior is to trash the terminal, but fixing it may lead to insight. Actually https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/4376 should fix it.
